covered_entities: those performing work and/or services for St. John's ("AI users")
covered_systems: AI tools including generative AI (e.g. ChatGPT, Bard)
covered_activities: use of AI for work-related activities on University, personal or third-party devices
exceptions: non-public data may be used in vendor-developed AI tools approved by the Administrative Technology Governance committee and reviewed by OIT

objective: Establish guidelines for the appropriate use of AI in the workplace that embrace innovation while complying with law and respecting privacy, confidentiality and data security.

clauses.original_text: These technologies must not be used to create content that is inappropriate, discriminatory, deceptive, or otherwise harmful to others or to the University.
clauses.actor: AI users (employees and those performing work for St. John's)
clauses.object: inappropriate, discriminatory, deceptive or harmful content
clauses.requirement: no harmful, discriminatory or deceptive AI-generated content
clauses.purpose: ethical use consistent with professional conduct and non-discrimination policies
clauses.applicable_systems: AI tools (including generative AI) used for work-related activities on any device

clauses.original_text: All AI-generated content must be carefully reviewed for accuracy, appropriateness, and bias before relying on it for work purposes.
clauses.requirement: review AI output for accuracy, appropriateness and bias before relying on it
clauses.condition: before relying on it for work purposes
clauses.purpose: accuracy and fairness of work products
clauses.applicable_systems: AI tools (including generative AI) used for work-related activities on any device
clauses.interpretation_notes: Reinforced in the guideline on inaccurate and biased information: fact-checking is necessary before answers are used in decision-making.

clauses.original_text: AI users are prohibited from inputting data specific to St. John’s University, including confidential or proprietary business information belonging to the University when using commercially, publicly available AI tools. This includes but is not limited to copying, pasting, typing, or in any way submitting personal information (e.g., names, contact information, dates of birth, social security numbers, etc.) about employees, students, and other members of the St. John’s community into AI tools.
clauses.object: University-specific, confidential or proprietary data and personal information
clauses.requirement: no University-specific, confidential or personal data in public AI tools
clauses.condition: when using commercially, publicly available AI tools
clauses.purpose: protect confidentiality, privacy and data security
clauses.affected_asset: personal information of employees, students and community; University confidential information
clauses.interpretation_notes: Followed by: inputs must be anonymized, and users must comply with the University's Information Technology (series 900) policies.

clauses.section: Policy - Data privacy, confidentiality and security
clauses.original_text: Only data classified as low risk (including public data) in accordance with the University’s Policy 922 - Information Classification Policy, may be used in AI tools and services. … Any other data classified as non-public may only be used in vendor-developed AI tools only after such tools have been approved by the Administrative Technology Governance committee and reviewed by the Office of Information Technology.
clauses.requirement: only low-risk data in AI tools; non-public data only in approved, IT-reviewed vendor tools
clauses.exception: non-public data in vendor-developed AI tools approved by the Administrative Technology Governance committee and reviewed by OIT
clauses.purpose: protect sensitive data in line with privacy and security laws
clauses.applicable_systems: AI tools (including generative AI) used for work-related activities on any device
clauses.interpretation_notes: Markdown link formatting removed from the policy name. Framed as one of the 'guidelines to be evaluated and followed prior to using any AI products or tools'.

clauses.original_text: Departments interested in using these tools must secure approval from the Administrative Technology Governance committee, as well as a security review by the Office of Information Technology.
clauses.action: secure approval and security review for
clauses.recipient: Administrative Technology Governance committee; Office of Information Technology
clauses.requirement: governance approval and IT security review before deploying vendor AI tools
clauses.condition: when departments want to use vendor-developed AI products
clauses.purpose: deploy vendor AI with appropriate guardrails

clauses.original_text: Before using AI for work purposes, AI users should discuss the parameters of their use with their direct supervisors. AI use in work should always be disclosed, and AI users must not plagiarize or fail to attribute AI-generated content that is used for work purposes.
clauses.object: AI use and AI-generated content in work
clauses.requirement: discuss AI use with supervisor, disclose AI use, and attribute AI-generated content
clauses.condition: before and when using AI for work purposes
clauses.applicable_systems: AI tools (including generative AI) used for work-related activities on any device
clauses.interpretation_notes: Mixed modality: discussion and disclosure are 'should', the ban on plagiarism/non-attribution is 'must not'.
